title: Mitigate stale/backfilled events causing skewed per-model breakdowns and percentile charts
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Problem: Over the last quarter we've had multiple incidents where late/retroactive ingestion (log replays, late Kafka partitions, or manual backfills) produces large, post-facto adjustments to per-model breakdowns and percentile latency/cost charts in the Console. These corrections appear as sudden spikes or drops in the UI and are confusing to customers and SREs.

Scope: This ticket focuses on Console time-series and percentile charts (p50/p95 token latency, tokens-per-request distributions) and top-model breakdown widgets that pull from the primary usage materialized views. It does not change billing LEDGER semantics; the goal is correctness and explainability of Console analytics only (though approaches should be compatible with billing reconciliation jobs).

Observed failure modes: 
- Late events double-count when ingestion retries reindex older batches without idempotency fingerprints.
- Backfill bursts overwrite rolling-window aggregates without a stable watermark, causing percentiles to jump for prior days.
- Console charts refresh immediately on ingestion and surface corrections indistinguishably from real traffic spikes.

Impact: Customers raising support tickets for perceived billing anomalies, engineers chasing no-op incidents, and reduced trust in Console charts for capacity planning.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console per-model breakdowns and p50/p95 charts must never show >5% visual delta for historical windows due to backfills older than the configured watermark window (default 72h).
2) When late/backfill corrections occur, Console must display a clear annotation ("backfill/reconciliation applied") and a consolidated delta row accessible from the chart.
3) Reconciliation job and ingestion must be idempotent: repeated replays of the same source batch produce no duplicate deltas in Console.
4) End-to-end integration test that simulates 50k backfilled events and validates chart deltas are limited and annotated.
5) Dashboard widget unit tests + one manual QA run on staging replicating prior incident pattern.
solution_outline:
Proposal (phased):
Phase A (short-term shielding):
- Introduce an ingestion watermark for Console analytics pipeline: events with event_time < now() - BACKFILL_TTL (default 72h) are accepted but routed to a "historical-adjustments" topic instead of live aggregates.
- Live charts continue to roll up in real-time; historical-adjustments are applied by a reconciling batch job that computes deltas and writes correction records to a 'corrections' store (idempotent).
- When corrections exist for a chart time window, the frontend overlays a discrete annotation and exposes the corrections delta row in the breakdown.

Phase B (reconcile + idempotency):
- Add an ingest_id fingerprint to every upstream event (hash of source, sequence, event_time). Ingestion deduplicator will drop exact duplicates.
- Reconciliation job computes per-model per-window deltas by comparing current aggregates to historical-adjustments snapshots and emits a single correction event per window. Corrections have a stable correction_id (idempotent key).

Phase C (long-term smoothing):
- Implement shadow-rollups that run every 24h computing an alternate aggregated timeline including corrections; use this to drive percentile smoothing and to optionally let customers opt into 'reconciled' view in Console.

Engineering trade-offs:
- Shielding via routing reduces visual noise quickly with low risk but delays visibility of corrected totals in live charts.
- Full idempotency requires upstream changes and coordination with ingestion teams; this is required for long-term correctness.
migration_plan:
1) Deploy watermark-routing logic behind feature flag in staging; route events older than 72h into historical-adjustments topic.
2) Deploy simple reconciliation worker that reads historical-adjustments and emits corrections to a corrections table (write-once semantics using correction_id).
3) Frontend: add annotation layer + corrections drawer; feature flag off-by-default.
4) Run controlled backfill simulation in staging using synthetic data (see tests) and iterate on thresholds.
5) Gradually enable feature flag in production for <5% of orgs, monitor, then rollout to all.
6) Once upstream teams add ingest_id, enable deduplication and remove temporary TTL heuristics if safe.

Rollback plan: disable routing feature flag (historical events revert to live aggregates) and delete any corrections emitted in the window if needed. Corrections writes are tagged with deployment id to ease removal.
monitoring_and_tests:
- Add Prometheus metrics: historical_routed_events_total, corrections_emitted_total, corrections_apply_failures, dedupe_drops_total.
- Add Console healthcard that surfaces number of pending historical adjustments and last successful reconciliation run time.
- Integration test harness: replay pipeline with controlled event_time skew and assert corrections emitted and chart deltas within threshold.
- Add e2e test that exercises frontend annotation and corrections UI using a staging snapshot.
- Post-rollout alert: if corrections_emitted_total / ingested_total > 0.02 for 24h, page on-call engineer for investigation.

Open questions: 
- Default BACKFILL_TTL (72h) was chosen to minimize normal out-of-order ingestion but needs product sign-off for customer expectations.
- UX: should we offer a toggle for 'show reconciled view' vs 'live view'? PM feedback pending.

Related: This work should coordinate with billing reconciliation scope but will not alter charged ledger rows until billing team signs off.
